`fetchWithTimeout` always overwrites `init.signal` with its own `AbortController` signal. If a caller passes a signal (e.g., request-scoped cancellation), it will be ignored. Consider wiring the provided signal to abort the internal controller (or merging signals) so both timeout and caller cancellation are respected.

When retrying on a retryable HTTP status, the previous `Response` body is neither consumed nor cancelled before waiting and retrying. In Node/undici this can prevent connection reuse and cause resource leaks under repeated retries. Before `await sleep(...)`/`continue`, explicitly drain or cancel the body (e.g., `response.body?.cancel()` or `await response.arrayBuffer().catch(...)`).

The docstring says Retry-After header support, but the implementation only supports the delta-seconds form via `parseInt(...)`. `Retry-After` can also be an HTTP-date; currently those will be ignored and fall back to exponential backoff. Either implement HTTP-date parsing or clarify the comment to avoid promising unsupported behavior.

`fetchWithRetry` doesn’t validate `maxAttempts`/`baseDelayMs`. If `maxAttempts` is 0 or negative, the loop won’t run and the function throws a generic error; negative delays will also behave unexpectedly. Add parameter validation (e.g., require `maxAttempts >= 1` and `baseDelayMs >= 0`) and throw a clear error early.

`fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort timer in `.finally(...)` as soon as `fetch()` resolves, but `fetch()` resolves when headers arrive (before the body is fully read). Call sites then parse the body with `response.text()`/`response.json()`, so an upstream that sends headers and stalls the body can still hang indefinitely and bypass the new timeout behavior.

The retry branch continues on 429/5xx without consuming or canceling the current response body. In Node's undici-based fetch, unread bodies hold connection resources until drained/canceled, so repeated transient failures can degrade connection reuse and cause avoidable request stalls under load.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Support HTTP-date Retry-After values**

The retry delay parser assumes `Retry-After` is always numeric seconds, but HTTP allows either `delay-seconds` or an absolute HTTP-date. When providers return a date value, `parseInt(...)` produces `NaN` and the code falls back to a short jittered delay, which can retry far earlier than instructed and prematurely exhaust attempts during rate limiting or maintenance windows.

These calls now retry POST image-generation requests after timeouts/5xx, but no idempotency key is attached, so a timed-out first attempt that was actually processed server-side can be executed again on retry. export const fetchWithTimeout = (url: string, init: RequestInit, timeoutMs: number): Promise<Response> => {
	const controller = new AbortController();
	const upstreamSignal = init.signal;
	const onUpstreamAbort = () => controller.abort();

	if (upstreamSignal?.aborted) {
		controller.abort();
	} else {
		upstreamSignal?.addEventListener('abort', onUpstreamAbort, { once: true });
	}

	const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);
	return fetch(url, { ...init, signal: controller.signal }).finally(() => {
		clearTimeout(timer);
		upstreamSignal?.removeEventListener('abort', onUpstreamAbort);
	});
};
